Perturbing and updating parameters by layer, zone and vegetation class#

A data assimilation run needs an ensemble: many copies of the model whose parameters and initial state differ. The scenario.toml file describes how those differences are drawn (the perturbation), and which of the perturbed parameters the observations are allowed to change (the update).

  • How a scenario is written

  • What a control applies to

  • Parameter catalogue and supported layouts

How a scenario is written#

A scenario is a table of lists. Every list is aligned with per_name: the i-th entry of each list describes the i-th parameter.

Key

Type

Meaning

per_name

list of str

Parameters to perturb (see the parameter catalogue below). A name may appear only once.

per_nom

number, or list

Nominal value (the value of the unperturbed model).

per_mean

number, or list

Mean of the distribution the ensemble is drawn from (usually the nominal value).

per_sigma

number >= 0, or list

Standard deviation (same unit as the parameter). 0 gives no spread.

per_type

"None", "additive", "multiplicative"

"None": the draw is the parameter. "additive" / "multiplicative": the draw is added to / multiplies the nominal value. A single value per Feddes parameter, a list per entry for soil parameters controlled by layer, zone or class.

sampling_type

"normal", "lognormal", "uniform"

Distribution of the draw.

transf_type

"None", "log", "log-ratio", "hyperbolic"

Transform applied before the analysis and inverted after it, to keep a parameter in its physical range ("log" for a positive one, "log-ratio" for a bounded one).

per_bounds

optional

Physical bounds, see Bounds below.

pert_control_name

optional

What an entry applies to: "layers", "zone", "root_map", or "None" (the whole domain). TOML has no null: write the string "None".

listUpdateParm

list of str

What the observations may change: "St. var." (the state) and the keys of the perturbed parameters ("Ks0", "ZROOT0"…).

What a control applies to#

The soil table is indexed by (zone, layer). A parameter perturbed with a control becomes one entry per layer, zone or class, and each entry writes some rows of that table.

Control

Keys

Rows of the soil table written by entry k

none

Ks (one key)

every row

layers

Ks0, Ks1…

layer k, in every zone

zone

Ks0, Ks1…

zone number k + 1, in every layer

root_map

Ks0, Ks1…

the zones that contain vegetation class k + 1, in every layer

Warning

The index k in a key is 0-based, but zone and class numbers are 1-based: Ks0 is zone 1. Zone and class numbers must run from 1 to K without gaps, and the nodata value -9999 of a map is not a zone.

Warning

Entries are written in order into the same table. When a vegetation class spans several zones, the entries of different classes overlap and the last one written wins: with classes 1 to 3 over two zones where class 2 covers both, Ks0 is overwritten by Ks1 in zone 1, and perturbing or updating Ks0 then has no effect. scenario.describe_ensemble lists these overlaps.

Parameter catalogue and supported layouts#

Not every parameter accepts every control. The table below was measured on the real perturbate() (test_scenario_layouts.py); a layout marked fails raises an obscure error inside the sampler, and validate_scenario reports it by name before the run.

Parameter

Writes

Controls

Layout of per_nom, per_mean, per_sigma

Ks

PERMX, PERMY, PERMZ together (isotropic)

none, layers, zone, root_map

scalar without control; a list with one entry per layer, zone or class with one

porosity

POROS

none, layers, zone (not root_map)

as Ks

n_VG, thetar_VG, SATCELL_VG

VGNCELL, VGRMCCELL, VGPSATCELL

none, layers, zone, root_map

as Ks

alpha_VG

nothing (no soil column is mapped to it)

not usable: it builds and samples, but writing it into the member soil files fails with Unknown parameter; perturb SATCELL_VG instead. The validator rejects it

ic

initial pressure head

none, layers, zone (not root_map)

as Ks; the key is ic (scalar) or ic0, ic1…

WTPOSITION

water table position

none only

scalar

ZROOT, PCREF

Feddes table

ignored (rows are vegetation classes)

scalar if the Feddes table has one row, otherwise a list with one entry per row

PCWLT, OMGC, PZ

Feddes table

ignored

scalar only: one nominal for every row, sampled independently per row (a list fails)

VGP

nothing

not implemented: its perturbation is commented out, the validator rejects it

A list without a control (Ks with per_nom = [1e-4, 1e-5] and no pert_control_name) fails for every soil parameter and for ic.

Keys. The key of a perturbed entry is what listUpdateParm must name: Ks for a scalar Ks; Ks0, Ks1… for lists; ZROOT0, ZROOT1… for the rows of the Feddes table (ZROOT0 even when there is one row). For Feddes parameters the index is the row position in the Feddes table (vegetation class order, 0-based), which is not the rule of the soil parameters (veg_map == k + 1).

Bounds#

per_bounds is optional and takes one entry per parameter: "None", a table { min = a, max = b } (either key may be omitted, the missing side is open) or a pair [a, b]. For a parameter with several entries the entry may be one specification shared by all of them, or a list with one specification per entry.

Bounds act twice: the prior is drawn from the truncated distribution, and every analysed value is clipped to the bounds after the update (members are kept, a warning lists the clipped values; rejecting them would shrink the ensemble). A malformed bound, or min >= max, is an error: it used to be ignored silently, leaving the parameter unbounded.

Examples#

The examples assume a model with 2 layers, 2 zones and 3 vegetation classes; the line # model: feddes_rows=N gives the number of rows of the Feddes table.

A homogeneous soil (one value of Ks for the whole domain, one rooting depth):

# model: feddes_rows=1
[scenario.homogeneous]
per_name = ["Ks", "ZROOT"]
per_type = ["None", "None"]
per_nom = [1e-4, 0.4]
per_mean = [1e-4, 0.4]
per_sigma = [1e-5, 0.02]
per_bounds = [{ min = 1e-6, max = 1e-3 }, { min = 0.1, max = 1.5 }]
sampling_type = ["normal", "normal"]
transf_type = ["None", "None"]
listUpdateParm = ["St. var.", "ZROOT0"]

Two layers, each with its own conductivity and its own bounds; only the upper layer is updated:

# model: feddes_rows=1
[scenario.layers]
per_name = ["Ks"]
per_type = [["None", "None"]]
per_nom = [[1e-4, 1e-5]]
per_mean = [[1e-4, 1e-5]]
per_sigma = [[1e-5, 1e-6]]
per_bounds = [[{ min = 1e-6, max = 1e-3 }, { min = 1e-7, max = 1e-4 }]]
sampling_type = ["normal"]
transf_type = ["None"]
pert_control_name = ["layers"]
listUpdateParm = ["St. var.", "Ks0"]

Two zones (Ks0 is zone 1, Ks1 is zone 2), one bound shared by both:

# model: feddes_rows=1
[scenario.zones]
per_name = ["Ks"]
per_type = [["None", "None"]]
per_nom = [[1e-4, 1e-5]]
per_mean = [[1e-4, 1e-5]]
per_sigma = [[1e-5, 1e-6]]
per_bounds = [{ min = 1e-7, max = 1e-3 }]
sampling_type = ["normal"]
transf_type = ["None"]
pert_control_name = ["zone"]
listUpdateParm = ["St. var.", "Ks0", "Ks1"]

Three vegetation classes: a soil parameter by class (root_map) and the rooting depth of each class (a Feddes parameter: one list entry per row of the Feddes table):

# model: feddes_rows=3
[scenario.vegetation]
per_name = ["Ks", "ZROOT"]
per_type = [["None", "None", "None"], "None"]
per_nom = [[1e-4, 1e-5, 1e-6], [0.3, 0.5, 0.7]]
per_mean = [[1e-4, 1e-5, 1e-6], [0.3, 0.5, 0.7]]
per_sigma = [[1e-5, 1e-6, 1e-7], [0.02, 0.02, 0.02]]
per_bounds = ["None", { min = 0.05, max = 1.5 }]
sampling_type = ["normal", "normal"]
transf_type = ["None", "None"]
pert_control_name = ["root_map", "None"]
listUpdateParm = ["St. var.", "ZROOT0", "ZROOT1", "ZROOT2"]

Updating parameters#

listUpdateParm selects what an analysis may change. "St. var." is the state (the pressure head); every other entry must be the key of a parameter that was built, not a name from per_name: ["Ks0"] for a scalar Ks is an error (the key is Ks), and perturbate() says so, with a suggestion. A parameter that is perturbed but not listed stays at its sampled value for the whole run.

After each analysis, in this order: the analysed parameters are transformed back (transf_type), clipped to their bounds, checked for physical validity (a negative rooting depth, one deeper than the mesh, a run that CATHY could not complete, rejects the member, with the reason recorded in <project>_rejections.json), and written to the input files of each member.

Be careful with what the data can tell: a parameter to which the observations are insensitive (a rooting depth for a short ERT survey of bare soil) is moved only by sampling noise, so updating it is a source of error, not information.

Checking a scenario before running it#

from pyCATHY.DA.scenario import validate_scenario, describe_ensemble

errors, warnings = validate_scenario(
    scenario, nlayers=2, zone_raster=zones, veg_raster=veg, n_feddes_rows=3,
    raise_on_error=False)

table = simu.describe_perturbation(scenario["listUpdateParm"])
print(table[["key", "control", "target", "updated"]])
print(table.attrs["warnings"])          # overlapping writes

perturbate() runs the validator itself (validate_scenario=False skips it) and checks listUpdateParm against the keys it built. run_DA_sequential logs the same table, as Perturbed parameters:, at the start of a run.
